question.text: Corporate fixed deposits accepted under Section 76 of the Companies Act, 2013 are:

answer.text: Fully secured by the assets of the company and carry zero risk
Guaranteed by the Government of India through a deposit insurance scheme
Unsecured in nature and risky if the company defaults
Available only to institutional investors and NRIs

explanation.text: The Logic: Corporate fixed deposits accepted under Section 76 of the Companies Act, 2013 are unsecured deposits. The workbook describes them as unsecured in nature and risky for the investor if the issuing company defaults, because the depositor has no specific charge on the company's assets to fall back on. The Trap: Option A is incorrect because the workbook explicitly characterises these deposits as unsecured. Option B introduces a government guarantee that the workbook does not attach to corporate FDs under Section 76, and Option D invents an investor-category restriction that is not stated. Note: For Section 76 corporate FDs, stay with the two workbook attributes — unsecured in nature and risky if the company defaults — and avoid importing comparisons or insurance schemes that are not part of the cited text.
